account:
It is day 1 at six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. Today I should read the appointment book before eight o'clock office business, visit the mill at ten, and attend the great hall lighting inspection with the builder at eighteen hundred. The regular appointments also include lunch at home, council letters, afternoon tea with my neighbour, and a return to the office.

The unusual business I know about is freight's large order for two hundred loaves from the baker. According to the secretary, freight called it his own order and gave the baker twenty-four emeralds and seventy-two wheat. Another five hundred twenty-eight wheat were needed, with hauling to be arranged today. The reported mill price is two emeralds per hay bale, yielding nine wheat, but available stock, delivery terms, the order's purpose, and a firm deadline remain unconfirmed. I do not know whether freight represents anyone else. There is no evidence that this is town business, and I have authorized no treasury payment. At the mill I intend to establish the facts rather than assume anything improper.

The builder says the hall inspection concerns even lighting from the new lanterns. That is the only purpose I have been told; I have no evidence of another. My neighbour reported peaceful docks and said the baker explained the lights there as the oven glowing while bread baked. There are vague bridge and port rumours, but nobody has given me concrete information. The large bread order could be ordinary private provisioning, though I do not yet know whom it is meant to feed or why so much is wanted. I should ask directly and distinguish witnessed facts from rumour.
